saints.name: The Martyrs of Compiègne
saints.title: Carmelite Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: Sixteen Carmelite nuns who went to the guillotine singing during the French Revolution…
biography: In 1794, at the height of the Reign of Terror, the sixteen Discalced Carmelite nuns of the monastery of Compiègne were arrested, tried, and condemned for continuing to live their religious life in defiance of the Revolution's laws. They had offered themselves to God for peace in France and for the Church.

On the seventeenth of July they were taken to the scaffold in Paris, renewing their vows and singing the Salve Regina and the Veni Creator as one by one they mounted the guillotine, the prioress last of all. Ten days later the Terror collapsed with the fall of Robespierre. They were beatified in 1906 and canonized in 2024.
saints.knownFor: Their serene martyrdom and offering for the Church of France.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of the Martyrs of Compiègne (vatican.va)
